hypotheses: Socioeconomic factors influence community engagement in COVID-19 social distancing.
Political affiliation affects adherence to social distancing guidelines.
claim.statement: Lower per capita income and greater Republican orientation were associated with significantly reduced social distancing among U.S. counties.

data.source: Unacast, American Community Survey, MIT Election Data and Science Lab
data.wave_or_subset: Data from March 19-28, 2020 compared to a pre-COVID-19 reference week.
data.access_details: Data provided by Unacast for research use
data.notes: Anonymized cell phone data may not represent all users.

method.description: Cross-sectional study using anonymized cell phone data to analyze the association between socioeconomic and political factors and social distancing.
steps: Obtain social distancing data from Unacast.
Measure adherence as changes in average distance traveled March 19-28, 2020.
Analyze socioeconomic data from the American Community Survey.
Analyze political preferences from MIT Election Data and Science Lab.
Use cross-sectional ordinary least squares regressions.
method.independent_variables: Per capita income, 2016 county-level vote share for Trump
method.control_variables: State fixed effects, sociodemographic and labor market characteristics, rurality

results.summary: Lower income and greater Republican orientation are linked to reduced social distancing.

numerical_results.outcome_name: Social distancing increase due to income
Social distancing decrease due to political support for Trump

metadata.original_paper_title: Association of County-Level Socioeconomic and Political Characteristics with Engagement in Social Distancing for COVID-19
